headline: Break slides to Santa Rosa; Saturday is the triangle day
body:
Small-craft advisories cover the outer waters — Pt. Sal to Santa Cruz including Santa Rosa, and the outer waters including San Nicolas and Santa Barbara Islands — through late Saturday night, NW 20 to 25 kt with seas to 7 ft and patchy fog. The channel itself is not under advisory. In the triangle today it's WNW 6 to 13 kn and 3.3 ft, with the wind filling in mid-afternoon. Saturday is the softer window: 7 kn at dawn, near calm at midday, 9 kn WNW by three, seas 3.4 ft.

So Saturday's the day, but the temperature is against us. All three corners run warm — west 72.1, east 71.9, south point 70.3 — and nothing in the 64–68 band lies inside the zone. The break has slid northwest onto Santa Rosa Flats, 68.7 today and 67.7 Saturday, and that water is out of reach at 20 kn NNW and 5.2 ft. Osborn's SW flank at 71.0 and San Nicolas at 70.3 are warm side too. Start the triangle's south point, the coolest corner, and hunt bait rather than a line on the chart.
